items.claim: The span Ezek.25.1-Ezek.25.7 is a sound unit and its level is sound, but one ground stated for it is false on the bytes. The row calls the Ammon address at oshb:Ezek.25.2 the book's FIRST foreign addressee. An earlier foreign address already stands at oshb:Ezek.21.33 = web:Ezek.21.28, where the messenger formula is directed to the children of Ammon, inside the collection that precedes this one. What oshb:Ezek.25.2 is earliest for is narrower and true: of the nine set-your-face verses, it is the earliest whose target is a foreign nation, the four before it naming domestic targets (oshb:Ezek.6.2 the mountains of Israel, oshb:Ezek.13.17 the daughters of the prophet's people, oshb:Ezek.21.2 = web:Ezek.20.46 the south, oshb:Ezek.21.7 = web:Ezek.21.2 Jerusalem). Every reference here touches the renumbered chapter and is written dual for that reason, and any installed wording must be written dual too. The reference-mirror flag on this unit is answered, not repeated: every verse it names is either the far side of a seam that the two-sided rule requires the prose to name, or a member of a verse RANGE written inside the rejected-alternative sentence. None is an argued boundary claim left without a reference entry, so the flag reads as a mirroring gap in this cluster and not as a form defect.
items.both_sides: Close side of the collection seam: oshb:Ezek.24.27 ends on the 3mp recognition refrain and a samekh follows that verse, and because a refrain closes the unit before it, the Jerusalem-addressed sign-act ends there. Onset side: oshb:Ezek.25.1 carries the word-event onset in its strict 39-verse form with no date attached, and oshb:Ezek.25.2 turns the prophet's face to a foreign nation. The addressee-class shift at this seam therefore stands on its own evidence; only the priority wording fails. The earlier Ammon unit at oshb:Ezek.21.33-Ezek.21.37 = web:Ezek.21.28-Ezek.21.32 is cross-seam continuity evidence that has to be disclosed rather than contradicted. The internal seam candidate at oshb:Ezek.25.6 was also weighed from both sides: oshb:Ezek.25.5 ends on a 2mp recognition-family clause with its own samekh, which is refrain-grade, and a messenger formula following a refrain close is one of the two conditions that license a cut; but oshb:Ezek.25.6 opens with a subordinating particle and keeps the same 2ms addressee, carrying a second accusation-and-verdict cycle, and a Ezek.25.6-Ezek.25.7 unit would be two verses with no word-event of its own, which the under-size rule forbids. The merge is correct.

items.claim: The span Ezek.26.1-Ezek.26.6 is right and the held level is right, but three of the row's stated grounds do not match the artifacts. FIRST, the date at oshb:Ezek.26.1 gives a YEAR and a DAY of the month and names NO month - 'in the eleventh year, on the first of the month', and web:Ezek.26.1 reads the same - so describing it as a month-and-day dateline, and keying its signal as year-and-month, asserts a term the verse does not carry; of the fourteen year-bearing datelines, TWO give a day of the month with no month term, oshb:Ezek.26.1 and oshb:Ezek.32.17, while the other twelve name a month. SECOND, the span carries two formula classes the row discloses nowhere: the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.26.3, which the 122-verse list holds, and the utterance signature at oshb:Ezek.26.5, which the 81-verse list holds; the row names the 'behold, I am against you' idiom at oshb:Ezek.26.3 but not the messenger formula standing in front of it in the same verse, and names nothing at all at oshb:Ezek.26.5. THIRD, the rejected-alternative prose counts FOUR units in this chapter and then enumerates THREE spans; the inventory puts the messenger formula on four verses of the chapter (oshb:Ezek.26.3, 26.7, 26.15 and 26.19), so the digit and the enumeration are answering different objects. None of the three moves a boundary. The reference-mirror flag on this unit is answered, not repeated: every verse it names is either the far side of a seam that the two-sided rule requires the prose to name, or a member of a verse RANGE written inside the rejected-alternative sentence. None is an argued boundary claim left without a reference entry, so the flag reads as a mirroring gap in this cluster and not as a form defect.
items.both_sides: Onset side: oshb:Ezek.26.1 joins the year date to the perfect-form word-event, the hardest onset class, with oshb:Ezek.25.17's recognition refrain and its samekh behind it. Close side: oshb:Ezek.26.6 ends on the strict 3mp recognition refrain and a pe follows it, while oshb:Ezek.26.7 reopens with the messenger formula against the SAME addressee. That is the collision class in which the seam falls at the verse boundary after the close verse, and it is where this row puts it. The undisclosed signature at oshb:Ezek.26.5 does NOT pull the seam back: its 'for I have spoken' clause sits mid-verse and a further clause about plunder for the nations follows it, so it is paragraph-final and not row-final, and no parashah mark is recorded after oshb:Ezek.26.5. The disclosure is owed; the cut is not.
